transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/time: 2028-05-03 16:00 UTC
- Duration: 47m
- Attendees: Ava Lin (Redwood AE), Diego Morales (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (CatalystOps Head of ML), Jason Liu (CatalystOps Infra), Marta Kovac (CatalystOps SRE), Ethan Park (PM)

Auto-generated summary (may be rough): Customer wants p95 under 200ms for chat, ideally 150ms for streaming; exploring hosted for speed of POC but storing logs in-house is a hard req; will run benchmark harness

[00:00] Ava Lin: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I think we have about 45 minutes, quick intros, then Diego will walk through the perf approach and we'll map that to your p95 targets.
[00:14] Priya Nair: Hi, Priya here, we run a customer support assistant and real-time insights, main question is latency under load. We tried a few hosted endpoints but saw token spikes and tail latency.
[00:27] Jason Liu: Jason, infra, we'll need to know what burst capacity looks like, and if Redwood Dedicated can handle simultaneous streams without dropping p95.
[00:35] Diego Morales: Great, yeah I'll cover batching, KV cache and streaming optimizations. Just quick qualification: what's your target p95 for the streaming path?
[00:44] Ethan Park: We're targeting 150ms p95 for the streaming user-facing response for short prompts (<= 80 tokens), longer jobs ok to be slower.
[00:55] Marta Kovac: Also, our concurrency spikes to ~1.2k simultaneous streams during demos, sustained maybe 400 normal.
[01:05] Diego Morales: Good, that's helpful. For 150ms p95 on streaming at 1.2k concurrency, we typically look at a couple levers: optimized kernel selection, KV prefix caching for repeated contexts, and continuous batching if you can accept tiny batching windows.
[01:25] Priya Nair: Can you explain KV prefix caching again? Last call the term came out as KV cash in the notes so want to make sure we understand.
[01:33] Diego Morales: Sure, sorry transcript typo — KV cache. Basically when you have repeated prefixes or system prompts, we keep key-value attention cache entries so subsequent requests avoid re-doing full forward passes for the prefix. Cuts per-token compute a lot for streaming.
[01:48] Ava Lin: Quick note, hosting mode differences matter: Hosted gives fastest onboarding and shared cache benefits for cold starts; Dedicated gives predictable throughput and isolation; Private (VPC/on-prem) gives control for audit logs but you give up Redwood-managed multi-tenant optimizations.
[02:08] Jason Liu: For Private, we need HSM/KMS integration for keys. Do you have a reference topology?
[02:15] Ava Lin: Yes, I'll send our Private topology diagram and KMS integration notes after the call.
[02:21] Marta Kovac: Also SOC2 is non-negotiable for production.
[02:25] Ava Lin: We are SOC2 Type II. I'll include the control summary.
[02:29] Priya Nair: Back to perf — what does token/sec look like for the medium family models we tested? We saw 600 tokens/sec single stream but that is on your competitor infra so results varied.
[02:42] Diego Morales: For the model class you're describing, on Redwood Dedicated with A100-class equivalents we usually see 1k-1.6k tokens/sec single stream depending on quant, sequence length, and beam settings. But for streaming p95 you care about head latency and small-token flushes more than pure tokens/sec.
[03:00] Jason Liu: How much does quantization change p95 vs end-to-end quality? Our ML team worries about hallucination shifts.
[03:09] Diego Morales: Quantization can reduce latency substantially — 16-bit int to 4-bit can cut per-token time, but you absolutely need evals against your prompts. Redwood Optimize recommends profiles per workload; we'll suggest a quantization candidate set and run quality checks with your prompt suite.
[03:29] Ethan Park: Can we run a benchmark with our actual prompts? The sample we used in-house didn't capture nested system prompts.
[03:36] Diego Morales: Yes — best practice: run both generation and streaming traces with your real prompt distribution. Diego: we'll provide the harness (Docker + k6 script) so you can run locally or we can run in our lab against Dedicated.
[03:50] Priya Nair: If you run it in your lab, how do we trust the numbers match our Private deployment?
[03:57] Ava Lin: Good question. Lab runs give a baseline. For Private, we supply a runbook and can run a joint benchmark in your VPC or on-prem during a pilot. Differences mostly come from networking and storage latency for KV loads.
[04:15] Jason Liu: What's the expected warm-up behavior? Our traffic is spiky and we hate cold-start tail latency.
[04:22] Diego Morales: For streaming, continuous batching and keeping a hot pool of sessions reduces cold-start. On Dedicated we recommend a small reserved pool of GPU reservations for hot paths; on Hosted we maintain global pools and use caching — but your SLA needs determine reserved vs shared.
[04:41] Priya Nair: SLA question — if we commit to Dedicated, what's the p95 guarantee?
[04:47] Ava Lin: Our Dedicated SLAs are latency-band-based per model class; for specific p95 numbers we map to model + sequence distribution in the contract. We can commit to a latency SLO and penalty at negotiable levels once we have benchmark data.
[05:04] Marta Kovac: Do you support streaming with chunk size control? Sometimes we need smaller flushes to reduce client perceived latency.
[05:12] Diego Morales: Yes, chunking/flush controls are supported in the SDK; you trade-off throughput per GPU. We'll show you the tuning knobs in the harness.
[05:22] Ethan Park: What's the CPU/network side effect? Our infra team worries about network saturating at high concurrency.
[05:29] Diego Morales: Good point — per-connection bandwidth matters. Streaming at high concurrency multiplies small packets. We recommend HTTP/2 or gRPC with multiplexing and also per-route rate limiting. We'll include a sizing calc for NIC requirements.
[05:46] Priya Nair: Can we talk about fallback behavior? If a model variant is down or overloaded, how do we keep clients alive?
[05:53] Ava Lin: Smart routing supports fallback to lower-cost model variants or regional replicas. We can configure automatic fallback to a cached respond or a smaller model that preserves core semantics. There are guardrails to prevent quality cliffs.
[06:12] Jason Liu: Any examples from customers?
[06:15] Diego Morales: We had a healthcare customer that kept p95 under 250ms by using prefix caching for templated prompts and fallback to a distilled model for non-sensitive auxiliary tasks.
[06:28] Priya Nair: On security, when you say audit logs — what's included and retention options?
[06:34] Ava Lin: Audit logs include request/response headers, auth events, model version IDs; retention configurable per plan. For Private we can give full retention control in your S3 buckets or logging stack.
[06:47] Priya Nair: For the benchmark, we want to measure both streaming p95 and tokens/sec under sustained 1h run with bursts; can you prepare the exact scripts?
[06:56] Diego Morales: Yes — we'll provide a harness with two modes: steady-state and burst profile. We'll instrument token-level timings and p95, p50, p99.
[07:09] Ethan Park: Are there tooling dashboards? Our PM wants real-time charts.
[07:13] Ava Lin: Redwood Console has per-route latency and token cost breakdowns with live traces. We'll share a transient demo dashboard link after the call.
[07:22] Priya Nair: About costs — raw numbers for hosting vs dedicated? At what point does Dedicated make sense economically?
[07:29] Ava Lin: Typically when your steady-state token volume and concurrency justify reserved capacity. We do a cost model comparing pay-as-you-go hosted vs reserved GPU-hour in Dedicated; we'll run that with your forecast.
[07:40] Jason Liu: A lot of the traffic uses long context windows, ~2k tokens. How does that shift the p95?
[07:46] Diego Morales: Longer contexts increase memory pressure and KV management overhead; for streaming we often strip context on the server side with prefix caching to limit re-encode. Sequence length increases per-token latency too. We'll recommend gen-specific configs.
[08:05] Priya Nair: Any concerns with hallucinations after quantization? We'll need A/B tests in the harness.
[08:12] Diego Morales: Absolutely — we'll attach quality regression tests to the harness so you can see rouge/accuracy metrics and human-sampled checks.
[08:23] Marta Kovac: Can you run the benchmark in our VPC? That would give the most accurate numbers.
[08:29] Ava Lin: Yes, for pilots we do joint runs in the customer's VPC with a temporary agent and remote control. That requires an on-boarding window and network whitelisting.
[08:40] Priya Nair: Great. For the initial POC we probably will do Hosted to get quick time to value but with log forwarding to our S3 for auditing. If results show we need lower tail latency, we switch to Dedicated.
[08:55] Ethan Park: Is there a hybrid option? Some customers want Hosted for read-only features and Dedicated for high-sla streaming.
[09:02] Diego Morales: Yes, routing policies can split traffic by route, region, or user segment and route to Dedicated or Hosted.
[09:11] Jason Liu: About metrics — what do you capture at token level? We need per-token timestamps, kernel times, and network RTT.
[09:19] Diego Morales: Harness instruments per-token generation timestamp, decode time, batch wait time, and kernel execution time. Network RTT comes from client-side traces.
[09:29] Priya Nair: Can you include cost per 1k tokens in the benchmark? We need to show exec cost vs latency trade off.
[09:36] Ava Lin: We'll provide cost modeling with tokens/sec to cost curves across Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private.
[09:44] Marta Kovac: Our compliance team insists on SAML SSO and RBAC before production. How is that managed?
[09:51] Ava Lin: We support SAML SSO and fine-grained RBAC in Redwood Console. For Private, you can connect to your IdP directly.
[09:59] Priya Nair: Ok, timeline — we want a POC in two weeks if possible. Is that realistic?
[10:04] Diego Morales: If you share prompts and sample traffic shape today, we can spin up a lab Dedicated run and a hosted POC within ~10 business days.
[10:12] Ethan Park: We'll send the sample workload and peak windows by EOD.
[10:16] Priya Nair: For the benchmark harness, do you require specific client versions? We use a mix of Python and Node.
[10:22] Diego Morales: The harness supports both, and we supply k6 scripts for load generation; the SDKs are in Py and JS.
[10:30] Ava Lin: Quick interjection — Diego, can you briefly outline the run plan we'll send?
[10:34] Diego Morales: Sure, plan: 1) Dry-run local v bench with 10 concurrent streams to validate prompts; 2) Steady-state 1 hour at expected concurrency (400) with 5 x 1m bursts to 1.2k; 3) Burst-only profile with progressive ramp; collect p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, kernel times; 4) Quality regression tests; 5) Shared report and model recommendations.
[10:58] Priya Nair: Sounds good. Will you also include guidance on batch window tuning?
[11:03] Diego Morales: Yes small windows of 10-30ms can capture batching without harming perceived latency for streaming. We'll try a few settings in the run.
[11:15] Jason Liu: What about monitoring for anomalies during burst? We need alerts.
[11:20] Ava Lin: Console supports alerting on route-level p95 or token-cost anomalies and can send to PagerDuty/Slack.
[11:27] Priya Nair: Any red flags we should be aware of before running the benchmark?
[11:31] Diego Morales: Ensure you have representative prompt shapes and that your client flushes are realistic; empty or synthetic prompts produce optimistic perf numbers. Also note that model warm-up can take a few minutes to reach steady-state.
[11:46] Ethan Park: Can you demo a short run where we see the console? Might be helpful.
[11:50] Ava Lin: We can do a follow-up demo; I'll attach a transient demo link and schedule a 30m session.
[11:58] Priya Nair: For the POC acceptance criteria: p95 < 180ms for streaming on 80-token prompts, sustained 90% throughput at 400 concurrency, and failover to lower variant under overload while preserving core semantics.
[12:15] Diego Morales: Noted and we'll codify these into the runbook.
[12:20] Marta Kovac: Anything else on encryption in transit? We require TLS mutual auth for Private.
[12:26] Ava Lin: Mutual TLS supported for Private; Hosted supports TLS with customer-managed certs via our ingress if needed.
[12:35] Jason Liu: Do you have any recommendations on client-side buffering to hide small slack?
[12:40] Diego Morales: Client buffering of ~50-100ms can smooth jitter but increases perceived latency; it's a UX trade-off. We'll provide best-practices notes.
[12:54] Priya Nair: Ok let's recap and next steps.
[12:58] Ava Lin: Recap: Redwood to share harness, security pack, Private topology, demo dashboard link; CatalystOps to share prompts, traffic profile, and acceptance criteria. We'll run lab benchmarks and plan a VPC joint run if required.
[13:14] Ethan Park: I'll send the traffic profile and confirm availability for a VPC onboarding window.
[13:20] Ava Lin: Diego, action items?
[13:23] Diego Morales: I'll push the Docker harness, k6 scripts, and a short how-to doc by next Wednesday. Also will include suggested quant candidates and profiling dashboard.
[13:35] Priya Nair: Thanks all — this helps. Looking forward to the harness.
[13:39] Ava Lin: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with notes and calendar invites.
[13:44] (call ends)

References shared during call: [link] Redwood Private topology (will be shared by Ava), [link] transient dashboard demo (will be shared).

Note: Transcription contains minor mis-hearings (e.g., "KV cash" -> KV cache).
